verdict.rationale: The Omarchy Menu has a built-in, keyboard-driven Install section with curated popular apps: editors (VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text) and terminals ready to install. A hands-on user says installing software is easy and fast. This is a curated installer menu, not a browsable app store, and coverage beyond developer tools and terminals is undocumented. Missing for 10: a documented app-store-style catalog of general popular desktop apps, evidence of one-click (rather than menu or keyboard) installation, and documentation of catalog breadth beyond dev tools and terminals.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can install popular desktop apps with a single click from a built-in app store

citations.quote: Neovim is the default, with VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text, Helix, Vim, and Emacs ready to install.
